sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling of the complete observed path \(W=(X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4,D)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(D\), with treatment beginning after date \(2\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every mixing, conditional assignment, and transition probability in the proposal-specific model lies in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical thirty-two-cell path PMF is inverted over all thirty-two labeled one-collision branches; no relative alignment is selected before projection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 4 identifies the model parameters under RSM, M, and ID; Proposition 5 and Corollary 1 identify LTATT and aggregate ATT under the paper's stated TI--LT regular conditions.
Theorem 1 identifies type-specific initial distributions, transition kernels, and type probabilities up to a common permutation from four consecutive observations under Assumptions 1--3.
Sections 3.2--3.4 formulate model comparison, implicit observable constraints, identification, and bounding for polynomial latent-variable models through real quantifier elimination.
Cylindrical algebraic decomposition gives an exact quantifier-elimination method for formulas over real closed fields.
CAD-based real quantifier elimination has doubly exponential worst-case dependence on dimension, while other real-algebraic methods address selected tasks with different bounds.
A rational inverse and semialgebraic membership conditions characterize regular parts of a single binary hidden Markov model, with exceptional cases treated as lower-dimensional submodels.
Discrete causal bounds can be posed as polynomial programs and approximated by spatial branch-and-bound with certified outer bounds and \(\epsilon\)-sharpness.
Finite mixtures are exactly partially identified under an excluded source of mixture-weight variation using probability restrictions.
Criterion inversion yields confidence regions for identified sets and their images under stated pointwise and uniform conditions.

body.tldr: On the compact binary four-period latent-transition model, the singular case with distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one collided control terminal row admits an exact observable treatment. Terminal splitting reduces the forty-coordinate existential fiber to displayed ten-variable systems and exactly thirty-two collided-state, orientation, and relative-alignment branches. A Collins-style sign certificate is necessary and sufficient for branch feasibility and aggregate-ATT point identification; the associated exact algorithm returns the attained, possibly disconnected image with Thom-encoded endpoints, latent witnesses, and discarded-branch certificates. A relatively open singular sign chamber and a rational law with two separated ATT values show that the geometry is not isolated. The contribution is this structural reduction and causal certificate grammar, not a generic CAD complexity improvement, a completion of the other collision patterns, or an overlap theorem for Ahn--Kasahara's regular class.

project_justification.gap: Ahn--Kasahara's parameter and ATT identification results impose their stated RSM, M, ID, and TI--LT regular conditions, while Higgins and Jochmans's four-observation Theorem 1 requires rank, type-separation, and connectivity conditions; neither classifies the one-collided-control-row merger stratum. Geiger--Meek and Collins supply general real quantifier elimination but leave the economically meaningful two-arm branch structure opaque.
project_justification.niche: Exactly one collided control terminal row is the first nonregular stratum on which full-path splitting, rank failure, probability-box contact, and relative treatment-control alignment interact but remain reducible to ten variables.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the reduction, gives the observable \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}\) classification, computes the exact attained ATT image on all thirty-two labeled branches, and supplies an open singular chamber plus rational disconnected benchmark.

body.related_work: Ahn--Kasahara is the closest econometric comparator in the same full-path latent-transition model: their Proposition 4 identifies the parameters under RSM, M, and ID, while their Proposition 5 and Corollary 1 identify LTATT and aggregate ATT under the stated TI--LT regular conditions. Those results inform the estimand and model architecture; no theorem here asserts equality on, inclusion in, or an extension of their regular class. Higgins and Jochmans's Theorem 1 identifies type-specific initial distributions, transition kernels, and mixing probabilities up to a common permutation from four consecutive observations under Assumptions 1--3: the observable matrices have the required rank, return-walk profiles separate types, and a common reference state is connected to every other state. That theorem supplies the closest four-observation Markov-mixture identification benchmark, but it does not classify a two-treatment-arm transition-alignment fiber when one control terminal row collides, project an aggregate ATT image, or reconstruct its endpoint representations. Critch's binary hidden Markov geometry motivates rational splitting and semialgebraic membership, but it has neither two treatment arms nor a causal alignment functional. Geiger and Meek provide the methodological bridge: Theorems 1 and 2 in Section 2 state real quantifier elimination and semialgebraic projection, while Sections 3.2--3.4 formulate model comparison, implicit equality and inequality constraints, identification, and bounds for polynomial latent-variable models. Their machinery is generic and supplies neither the two-arm transition-alignment fiber, the observable one-collided-control-row branch certificate, a causal ATT image, nor reconstructed endpoint representations. Collins's cylindrical algebraic decomposition is the closest exact certification engine, and Basu's survey fixes the relevant worst-case complexity benchmark; the gain here is solely the proved structural dimension reduction and branch-labeled causal output. Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser motivate polynomial optimization for sharp discrete causal bounds, but their general routine returns successively refined outer bounds rather than the present exact attained semialgebraic image. Henry, Kitamura, and Salanie characterize a different exclusion-driven finite-mixture set. Romano--Shaikh motivates set inversion; the auxiliary coverage result here is finite-sample and deliberately excludes Hausdorff or endpoint-persistence claims.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The completed object is the stratum with distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one collided control terminal row. Laws whose global compact fiber also contains representations from another collision pattern are outside this class. The certificate uses exact Collins-style projection after model-specific reduction and may retain the generic worst-case cost of real quantifier elimination.
body.honest_scope: The quotient semantics, forty-to-ten reduction, thirty-two-branch classification, exact stratum-restricted region, disconnected benchmark, and finite-sample coverage are to be proved. The remaining open content is whether the complete CAD projection list can be compressed to a smaller irredundant and interpretable observable sign basis. Ahn--Kasahara's regular identification results are comparators only: no internal overlap-equality, model-inclusion, or regular-chart theorem is claimed. No result is claimed for the other terminal-collision strata, for an unboxed singular class, or for Hausdorff consistency.
